# Dependency direction and service ownership

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `architecture-boundaries` · **Architecture & Distributed Systems** · Catalog level: senior

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S01-Q042](#S01-Q042)

<p>Explain Clean Architecture through the dependency direction in a small application. How would you check that business rules do not accidentally depend on infrastructure details?</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Defend an application boundary and deployment shape from ownership and change requirements.</p>

<ul>
<li>Draw code dependencies separately from runtime collaboration.</li>
<li>Compare layered, Clean/Onion/Hexagonal and modular-monolith boundaries.</li>
<li>Justify data ownership and independent deployment against their operational cost.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

- [Dependency contracts and lifetime ownership](dotnet-di-solid.md)

<p>Begin with what may depend on what, then ask which capability owns the data and changes independently. The same boundary reasoning makes a microservice decision understandable without equating services with small codebases.</p>

<a id="S04-Q008"></a>

### S04-Q008 · Foundation

<p>What makes a system a microservice architecture beyond having many small services? Illustrate the defining responsibilities with one example.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q008](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q008)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q008](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q008)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Define microservices beyond “small services”.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain what the service boundaries enable, not a preferred service size. Separate independent responsibility from a diagram with many boxes.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Define microservices through architectural properties and consequences.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use a generic system; clarify business ownership and release behavior without assuming a particular platform.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connect the definition to ownership and the ability to change a service.</li>
<li>Recognize when separate processes still behave as a tightly coupled system.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Defining a microservice by line count or number of endpoints alone.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>Can two small services still require coordinated releases?</li>
<li>Which observation would show that a boundary is useful?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q004"></a>

### S04-Q004 · Mechanism

<p>Compare layered, Clean, Onion and Hexagonal approaches with a modular monolith. For one business operation, how would each choice shape dependencies and responsibilities?</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q004](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q004)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q004](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q004)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Compare layered architecture, Clean/Onion/Hexagonal approaches and a modular monolith.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Compare what the labels organize: code dependencies, access to infrastructure and application modules. Clarify where the approaches can coexist.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Reason about dependency structure without treating architecture labels as exclusive products.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use one application example; distinguish source-code boundaries from runtime deployment boundaries.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Trace a business operation across the proposed dependency boundaries.</li>
<li>Explain which change becomes easier and which complexity remains.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Assuming a modular monolith and Clean Architecture are mutually exclusive options.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you check that the intended dependency direction is respected?</li>
<li>What changes when a module must be deployed independently?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q007"></a>

### S04-Q007 · Mechanism

<p>What does data ownership mean when services must be independently deployable? Explain how another service may use that data without making every schema change a coordinated release.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q007](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q007)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q007](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q007)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain data ownership when services are independently deployable.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Focus on who can change authoritative data and who depends on its contract. Separate physical database placement from ownership rules.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Explain how data access contracts affect independent change.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Assume separate service releases; clarify whether shared storage, replicas or direct database access currently exist.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Identify who owns writes and the contract exposed to consumers.</li>
<li>Trace the impact of a schema change and propose a compatibility check.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Calling data private while other services freely modify its tables.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would consumers learn that the data has changed?</li>
<li>What would you do when a report needs data owned by several services?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S01-Q042 · Mechanism

<a id="S04-Q003"></a>

<p>Explain Clean Architecture through the dependency direction in a small application. How would you check that business rules do not accidentally depend on infrastructure details?</p>

**Source:** [S01-Q042](../../sources/01-csharp-dotnet.md#q042) · [S04-Q003](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q003)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S01-Q042](../../sources/01-csharp-dotnet.md#q042)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain Clean Architecture and dependency direction.

</div>

**[S04-Q003](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q003)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain Clean Architecture and dependency direction.

</div>

**Why these source prompts share a canonical question:** Identical Clean Architecture and dependency-direction prompt.

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Draw both code dependencies and runtime collaboration; they answer different questions. Relate the boundaries to replacing or testing a concrete external component.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Reason about architecture from dependency relationships and ownership.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use a hypothetical application, not a required folder template; preserve both the C# pattern context and the broader architecture source framing.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Names the owner of interfaces and traces a use case across the boundaries.</li>
<li>Explains a change or test that demonstrates the intended independence and its cost.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Treating folders or project names as proof that dependency direction is correct.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What would a compiler dependency check reveal that a runtime flow diagram would not?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q006"></a>

### S04-Q006 · Application

<p>Given a business workflow, how would you decide where one service ends and another begins? Show a boundary you would consider and explain how you would test it.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q006](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q006)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q006](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q006)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How do you identify service boundaries?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>A service boundary assigns responsibility for rules, data and changes. Explain your discovery process instead of starting from table names.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Derive service boundaries from business behavior and change coupling.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Choose a generic workflow; clarify ownership, consistency and deployment constraints before proposing a split.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connect the proposed boundary to business rules and data ownership.</li>
<li>Use change history or a workflow trace to challenge the proposed separation.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Creating one service per database table without examining the workflow.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What would frequent coordinated deployments reveal about the boundary?</li>
<li>How would you handle a rule that appears to cross both services?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q010"></a>

### S04-Q010 · Failure cases

<p>After a monolith is split into services, what new failure modes would you investigate? Trace one failure from its cause to the user-visible outcome.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q010](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q010)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q010](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q010)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What common failure modes appear after splitting a monolith?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Show how moving work across a network changes the failure boundary. Focus on a concrete chain rather than a catalog of pattern names.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Diagnose failure introduced by distributed responsibility.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Choose one generic workflow and distinguish the previous in-process behavior from the new service interaction.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explain how latency, partial success or communication failure affects the workflow.</li>
<li>Propose evidence that distinguishes a suspected cause from another plausible cause.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Assuming every service either succeeds or fails together.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What would the client observe if a service committed but its reply was lost?</li>
<li>How would you test this failure before production?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q005"></a>

### S04-Q005 · Trade-offs

<p>When would you keep a modular monolith instead of splitting it into microservices? What evidence would justify changing that decision?</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q005](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q005)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q005](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q005)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> When should a system remain a modular monolith rather than become microservices?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Compare keeping modules in one deployment with accepting separate service operations. Identify the problem that a split would actually solve.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose a deployment structure from business and operational constraints.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Assume either structure is feasible; establish team size, change patterns, scale needs and consistency requirements.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Compare independent deployment benefits with communication and operational costs.</li>
<li>Set a measurable trigger for reconsidering the decision rather than assuming growth requires a split.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Treating microservices as the inevitable next stage for every growing system.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>Which module would you separate first, and why that one?</li>
<li>What would make you cancel or reverse an extraction?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q009"></a>

### S04-Q009 · Trade-offs

<p>Which benefits would justify operating microservices for a particular system? Compare those benefits with the extra work your team would need to own.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q009](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q009)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q009](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q009)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What benefits justify the operational complexity?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Make the justification specific: a desired capability must outweigh a cost in the stated context. Avoid presenting every possible benefit as guaranteed.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Evaluate architectural value against operational responsibility.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State current bottlenecks, team capacity and deployment needs; no production scale or improvement is assumed.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Tie each claimed benefit to a real constraint and a way to verify improvement.</li>
<li>Account for deployment, incident handling and cross-service coordination costs.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Claiming better speed or reliability solely because services were separated.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What additional operational capability must exist before the split?</li>
<li>How would you know after six months whether the change was worthwhile?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>A hypothetical .NET application handles orders and reporting. One team proposes separate deployments. Draw a modular-monolith option and a split option, assign data owners, trace an update and identify a failure introduced by the split. State what evidence would justify the added operational work.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Explains dependency direction and names a coherent owner for each responsibility.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Defends the chosen boundaries, alternatives and consistency costs with a trace and validation plan.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>Service boxes or folder labels alone do not demonstrate independent ownership or a safer deployment.</p>
